body:
COMPANION to base ticket T-01KZXHSQSMJS92XWX3SPTV3GVS (operative-aware suppression-marker dodges). That ticket is already merged and its contract cannot be altered in a PR, so these two extensions — earmarked for it during the 2026-08-13 seam program but not in its body — land here. Build this AFTER or TOGETHER WITH that ticket so the operative-vs-inert machinery exists to extend. This ticket names markers DESCRIPTIVELY, never literally, because the suppression scan reads this ticket's own JSON (the exact defect being fixed).

PROBLEM (both halves observed in production):

1. TICKET-STORE PROSE FLAGGED AS OPERATIVE. rails-guard's suppression scan flagged PR #493 because a ticket BODY (JSON prose describing suppression markers) contained literal marker spellings. A marker inside `.adlc/tickets/**` or `.adlc/ticket-archive/**` shard JSON is descriptive text — it cannot suppress any test — yet the ticket had to be reworded (commit f331846) to dodge the gate. The scan already treats doc/MDX inert spans as inert; the ticket store deserves the same authoritative classification.
2. MARKERS MATCH OUTSIDE THEIR LANGUAGE. Each marker in the closed SUPPRESSION_MARKERS list (packages/rails-guard/lib/suppressions.mjs) is operative only in its own toolchain: the JS/TS skip and only test modifiers only in JavaScript/TypeScript sources, the TypeScript ignore/expect-error directives only in TS, the Python no-qa and type-ignore directives only in Python, and so on. Today a Python-only directive appearing in a .mjs file (for example inside a string) is flagged — a false positive that trains operators to distrust the gate.

BUILD

1. Classify `.adlc/tickets/**` and `.adlc/ticket-archive/**` files as inert-prose surfaces in the suppression scan (same mechanism as the existing doc/MDX handling — extend the isDocFile-style classification, do not special-case downstream).
2. Add a per-marker language map: each marker carries the set of file extensions where it is operative; a diff hunk in a file outside that set does not match. Derive the map from each tool's own documentation, and keep it beside SUPPRESSION_MARKERS so a new marker cannot be added without declaring its languages (fail closed: a marker with no declared languages is operative everywhere).
3. Do NOT weaken the operative paths: a real marker in its own language in a code file must still flag, and the base ticket's case-sensitivity contract is untouched.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- AC1: a ticket shard whose body contains any literal marker spelling is NOT flagged; the pre-reword body of the suppression ticket (reconstruct from git history of PR #493, commit f331846's parent) is the regression fixture. Verify: new test in packages/rails-guard/test/, named in the build.
- AC2: a Python-only directive added inside a .mjs file is NOT flagged; the same directive added in a .py file IS flagged. Verify: same test file.
- AC3: a JS skip modifier added in a .mjs test file IS still flagged (no weakening). Verify: same test file.
- AC4: a hypothetical marker registered with no language declaration is flagged in every file type (fail-closed default). Verify: same test file.
- AC5: suite green: npm test.

NOTES FOR THE BUILDER

- Enforcement-package change: tiers trust-root, needs a distinct-provider cross-model approve.
- No rails declared here (2026-08-14 lesson); freeze tests in-session during the build.
title: Suppression scan: treat ticket-store prose as inert and scope each marker to its own language
